Perastage Canonical MVR contract

Perastage Canonical MVR is the standards-valid MVR 1.6 representation of the current domain scene. Project scene.mvr, MVR-xchange, and read-only consumers use CanonicalMvrExportOptions() and the same serializer. The canonical truss representation is the standard MVR Symbol/Symdef representation. Every normal standalone export uses this policy, independently of saved compatibility preferences.

For an explicit Direct Geometry3D for truss symbols standalone export, the same serializer derives a compatibility representation from a private copy of the canonical scene. It expands supported Symbol/Symdef truss geometry into direct Geometry3D references without changing the live scene. This is an alternative standards-valid MVR 1.6 serialization: a Truss requires Geometries, whose graphical children may be either Symbol or Geometry3D. The option improves interoperability with applications whose Symbol/Symdef support is incomplete, but it is never project persistence, canonical snapshot, MVR-xchange, Inspector, or internal scene authority.

The canonical root contains at most one GeneralSceneDescription/UserData. That element contains one Data provider="Perastage" ver="1.0" block. Its versioned maps supplement scene fidelity, including fixture type information, ProjectFixtureMetadataMap, truss and hoist information, primitive geometry, and layer appearance. These maps never replace an official MVR or GDTF field and never contain local absolute paths. Supported Perastage fixture metadata is applied by project restore, replace/open, and merge imports. Entries are keyed to fixture UUIDs; the existing merge remapping then carries each imported fixture and its restored values to its collision-free identity without changing unrelated target objects. Unsupported versions and malformed entries remain non-fatal diagnostics.

Valid foreign root Data blocks are stored separately as opaque scene data. Perastage does not interpret them. Canonical export reparses each stored block, isolates malformed payloads as inert recovery evidence, omits anything claiming Perastage ownership, deduplicates repeated payloads, and places accepted blocks beside the single Perastage block under the one legal root UserData. Merge unions these blocks without accumulating duplicates. XML subtree serialization may normalize insignificant formatting, but preserves provider identity and XML structure.

MvrExporter::ExportCanonicalSnapshotToBuffer copies the supplied MvrScene and performs identity and transform recovery only on that copy. Snapshot and normal serialization therefore cannot mark the live project dirty or leak repairs into it. Resource leases are shared by the copy, avoiding duplication of resource payloads while keeping their lifetime safe.

Interactive project save and standalone export both call SyncSceneData() as an explicit command-boundary preparation step. This commits pending derived fixture type colors to the domain scene without reintroducing table-wide GUI resynchronization. Project save then requests the canonical policy. File > Export MVR starts with Use compatibility export for this file unchecked. The saved preference suggests the representation only after that explicit opt-in; it remains stored under its existing key. The dialog shows the transformation and passes explicit options to the same exporter. Cancelling or unavailable dialog customization leaves the canonical policy in effect. Direct Geometry3D derives only the standalone compatibility representation. Direct domain serialization and Inspector snapshots remain independent of GUI preferences and operate on the scene supplied by their caller.

The .pstg container continues to own application and workspace state outside scene.mvr: window perspectives, splitter positions, selections, preferences, toolbar state, caches, revision/dirty bookkeeping, and machine-specific paths. Only portable state that describes or supplements the scene belongs in MVR.

Layer UUIDs and object layerUuid ownership are authoritative. Names, including empty and duplicate names, are preserved independently; generated GUI labels never replace authored MVR names. The default layer has a canonical deterministic UUID before export. See Layer identity for default policy, legacy layer_default migration, workspace state, and compatibility boundaries.

Layer owns its MVR 1.6 vertical elevation and authored matrix precision. Scene node transforms are world-space; exported local matrices are relative to the immediate GroupObject or, for roots, the owning Layer. Import composes each parent once. Export preserves unedited numeric source values, repairs locals on a private snapshot after world-space edits, and may omit an identity Layer Matrix. Layer merge equality includes the authored matrix values. Publication projects non-elevation layers to elevation while retaining represented world placements and rebasing retained source children. Unrepresentable source values are disclosed.

Fixture, Support and Truss each own one optional standard Addresses collection with ordered DMX Address and Network lists (Address children precede Network), retaining container presence, optional break attributes and authored values. Missing break means 0; break IDs identify assignments and never universes. Fixture.address is the compatibility projection of break 0 only. Unedited nonzero-only or out-of-editor- range assignments remain preservable without an invented primary assignment. Core perastage::patch::SetFixturePrimaryPatch edits only break 0. Explicit patching of an absent/empty list creates it; clearing removes only it and retains the container/other entries. A missing primary in a nonempty list, duplicate breaks or invalid values produces a structured conflict. Existing table/auto-patch workflows use that policy; auto-patch publication is atomic. Pending legacy scalar edits reconcile only on a private export snapshot with an unambiguous mapping. A final serialized projection check protects the complete ordered list. Fixture Network retains required case-sensitive GDTF wire-geometry names and optional ipv4/subnetmask/ipv6/dhcp/hostname presence and text. Patch edits never modify this list. Names are not UUID references and are not remapped at merge. Publication validates each Network independently against the effective definition. An invalid or unresolved assignment is omitted with its exact values in a warning; independent DMX Address entries survive. Optional unusable Support/Truss bindings are omitted rather than given a fictitious mode. Required Fixture bindings use the caller's existing installed fallback profile and an actual declared mode when needed, with an explicit substitution warning. No GDTF file or mode is fabricated. Controlled rebind commands remain strict and atomic before editor mutation. Standard addressed Truss resources remain byte-preserved unless a validated canonical derivative is issued: final verification checks both source/output SHA-256 digests, the exact paths and actual WiringObjects/mode relationships. Type metadata edits are retained in explicit existing TrussInfo overrides; they never silently rewrite the authored standard GDTF. A unique legacy-native filename alias may be resolved in the scene resource directory before selecting a fallback. Imported source owners and explicit failed acquisition evidence never use that alias policy. Missing model/dependency references are omitted individually, preserving owners, placements and a valid empty Geometries container without invented replacement geometry. SceneObject-to-Truss conversion copies compatible identifiers, Classing and matrix provenance; retained source issues, FocusPoint, multiple models, Symbol ownership and nonidentity geometry cause atomic structured refusal. SceneObject Addresses, including empty presence, are retained by the validated source-field projection when their standard structure is valid. Fixture-to-Support conversion preserves the complete collection, Classing, standard identifiers (including CustomId/CustomIdType presence and explicit zero), GDTF binding, position, layer/group ownership and numeric matrix source. Legacy primary patch strings are materialized through the existing patch policy. Focus, Fixture Color, Pan/Tilt inversion, explicit project color/symbol/power or unresolved physical property overrides and retained source conflicts or missing required GDTF mode/binding return a structured field-specific refusal before mutation or Undo publication. Unresolved scene preservation evidence also blocks conversion: its source UUIDs survive merge remapping and may contain opaque references. Derived fixture metadata is not a new Support standard field; existing hoist load/function defaults remain intentional conversion semantics. No network settings are applied. Published Universe.Address strings and signed break IDs are preserved even where the unchanged pinned XSD's integer/nonnegative restrictions disagree.

Root UserData precedes Scene, as required by the official XSD. Every exported GroupObject retains ChildList, including empty groups, to satisfy the pinned XSD; published MVR 1.6 Table 22 permits its absence. These representation rules preserve standards-valid identity round-trips.

FocusPoint uses the existing geometric SceneObject value with a distinct SceneObjectKind::FocusPoint and is serialized with its standard element name. Direct geometry, ownership, transforms and Fixture Focus links share the existing identity/resource/mutation services. Symbol-based focus geometry retains standard Symbol UUIDs and references through the source-structure projection described below. A required Geometries container may be empty; no replacement mesh is invented for an empty focus.

Export preparation repairs a private snapshot before validating the actual projection. Recoverable source defects produce precise warnings after a real repair, omission or substitution; the validator still rejects invalid generated output. PSTG and MVR-xchange use that same preparation and serializer. Successful publication is not proof that every provider extension survives. See the coverage audit for protected structures, unresolved P0 losses and the official XSD/UserData discrepancy. Full-document XSD conformance must not be inferred from the internal structural validator or from successful export/reimport.

Classes are a persistent scene-wide UUID registry, independent of layers. Each supported Fixture, GroupObject, FocusPoint, SceneObject, Truss and Support owns its optional direct Classing UUID. Export retains unused definitions and exact optional names; equal names never identify or coalesce classes. Merge remaps real identity collisions and incoming references together, including cross-kind collisions regardless of object replacement policy. Malformed/duplicate source Class identities receive deterministic occurrence identities; uniquely resolvable Classing targets are updated together. Genuinely ambiguous/unresolved Classing relationships are omitted with a precise warning, without discarding unrelated definitions or objects. A final projection check continues to reject accidental serializer omissions.

This preserves the identity model needed for future class visibility filtering across layers in Viewer2D, Viewer3D and Layout Mode. There are no visibility controls or flags in this change. Visibility presets and documentation settings will belong to PSTG, without adding proprietary Class attributes to MVR.

Preservation, canonicalization and controlled repair

Symdef collection distinguishes definition identities from Symbol occurrence identities and symdef targets. Repeated instance UUIDs, including UUIDs shared with their definition, do not invalidate an independently identifiable Symdef. Import resolves its model geometry before returning the typed scene, then uses the canonical occurrence repair for native projections and retained source XML together. Already valid instance identities remain unchanged. Genuine duplicate definitions and collisions with other standard nodes remain diagnosed. Repeated project/canonical saves retain the repaired identities and original model bytes.

Preservation protects valid authored information and meaning, including fields without an editor. Canonicalization may change representation: standard element ordering, equivalent numeric spelling, resource packaging with consistent reference rewriting, identity layer matrices, empty optional assignment containers, and required XSD containers. It does not authorize changing arbitrary text, precision, identities or relationships. XML whitespace in otherwise empty optional assignment containers, including character references, is insignificant; attributes, child elements and non-whitespace text remain protected. This is a bounded rule, not permission to discard unknown fields.

For the same scene and effective canonical options, PSTG scene.mvr and standalone canonical output must have exactly the same ordered ZIP entry names and uncompressed bytes, including XML text, attributes, values and element order. ZIP metadata and compression may differ. This compares two generated outputs, not generated output with imported XML. Project documentation, styles, visibility presets and preferences belong outside scene.mvr.

FixtureID and FixtureIDNumeric are selection labels, independent of persistent UUID identity. Authored duplicates, zero, empty strings and optional presence retain the bounded #2484 policy. Future allocation/duplicate repair must be an explicit reusable plan, with diagnostics and Undo/Redo when applied to the live scene. Import repair changes state at an explicit command boundary; canonical export only derives a private snapshot; compatibility export is a named alternate operation. None may consume future repair preferences implicitly.

Canonicalization operates on a private export snapshot. Recoverable import anomalies must be repaired or projected with precise warnings rather than turning semantic preservation checks into a general save veto. The implemented rules are deliberately narrow:

Input Canonical action Diagnostic
Repeated modeled source UUID on import Apply the existing occurrence-level resolver result to typed objects and retained XML before Classing/topology capture Import log records occurrence, old/new UUID and placement
Earlier-session repeated SceneObject source owners Reconcile with actual imported identities using the existing resolver or unique retained local-matrix provenance Warning / IdentityChanged; resources and Class targets unchanged
Absent or XML-whitespace-only optional GDTF pair Omit the empty optional pair Equivalent normalization
Incomplete substantive Truss/Support optional binding Omit the binding and dependent Network assignments, retaining DMX Address entries, geometry and other object data Warning / DataOmitted with values and owner/field
Complete substantive optional binding Preserve authored Spec/Mode and resource relationships Existing resource/reference validation
Archive/serialization/publication failure Fail truthfully; retain previous destination and dirty state Error

The official 1.5 text lists Truss GDTFSpec as optional and GDTFMode as required; the 1.6 Table 28 makes both optional, with Mode mandatory when a substantive Spec is defined. The reader accepts older empty pairs permissively and emits the supported 1.6 representation; the input fixtures are checked against the pinned 1.6 XSD, not claimed to satisfy a separate historical 1.5 schema.

No GDTF mode, definition, reference target or geometry is invented by these rules. Newly imported topology uses the same per-XML-node identity decisions as the typed reader. Earlier-session recovery never allocates another editable identity and never rewrites model filenames based on UUID substrings. The imported archive remains byte-identical. Export warnings use the existing structured diagnostic/log and MVR result dialog; no ignore-preservation option or alternate PSTG scene serializer is added.

The publication repair service distinguishes equivalent normalization, identity repair, specific omission/substitution and fatal technical failure. It does not change all Error severities to Warning. Only the repaired snapshot is serialized; strict pure validators still expose defects on the unmodified imported scene.

Additional recoverable case Published result
Valid integer beyond native editor range Preserve lexical standard integer; explicit native edits win
Invalid scalar/source-only field Publish the represented editable value; identify exact original field/value
Missing geometry/media or invalid relationship Omit only that reference/payload; retain independently valid objects/resources
Repeated Symbols, missing/cyclic Symdef edge Repair occurrence identities or remove only the unsatisfiable edge
Nonfinite numeric component or broken ownership Substitute only unrepresentable component or detach invalid parent; retain finite world placement
Unknown top-level GDTF FixtureType payload Explicit canonical projection retains standard fields/resources; removed original XML is disclosed
Physical power change without a standard write owner Keep authored profile and explicit per-fixture planning metadata; warn that external physical patch was not performed

Material findings are stored as inert escaped text in permitted root Data provider="org.perastage.canonical-recovery" ver="1". Reopen retains and logs them; known extraction-directory prefixes become relative resource references in stored disclosures while local diagnostics retain full context. Evidence is never executed, reconciled automatically or treated as a second editable scene. Missing resource bytes cannot be reconstructed from a warning: the original imported package remains the recovery source. Existing application-owned planning metadata preserves native power/weight values and TrussInfo explicitly distinguishes type overrides from GDTF source authority. Canonical derivative revisions omit the optional generated Date, retaining all authored revision dates, so wall-clock time does not change canonical payloads.

Coverage remains bounded by executed synthetic/regression cases. New unknown provider structures require actual projection tests; there is no catch-all ignore-preservation flag or promise that a corrupt/unwritable archive succeeds.

Valid source-only fields of Fixture, Truss, Support and SceneObject have a focused export projection: the retained XML is validated against its existing MVR 1.6 type, attached to the matching generated UUID owner and written in standard child order. This includes CastShadow, protocols, commands, alignments, connections, mappings and other fields listed in mvr_standard_field_projection.cpp. MappingDefinition is retained under AUXData. Source references must resolve; source resources use the normal resource collection. Merge remaps retained owner UUIDs and standard references, including equivalent uppercase/lowercase UUID spellings, along with resource paths. No source fragments are executed or injected into the editable scene, and no schema extensions are added. Deletion of a modeled owner deletes its retained fields. An editable/source field conflict is diagnosed rather than choosing a value silently. Reopening reconstructs the evidence from the canonical scene.mvr, so later saves and standalone canonical exports follow exactly the same policy.

Save preparation rolls back scene, layouts, resources, preferences and dirty state on failure. Archive publication closes the temporary file then replaces the target atomically on the same filesystem; there is no overwrite-by-copy fallback. Save As commits its session path only on confirmed success. A failed save exposes all export findings in the dialog's expandable details after the busy overlay has closed.

Retained standard scene structure

mvr_source_structure_* owns a versioned, immutable scene-local provenance value. It retains shallow standard node payloads, authored local/world matrices and editable display baselines. VideoScreen/Projector payloads, media, multipatch, parametric ChildList ownership and Symbol geometry are validated against the existing standard types. They are restored around the ordinary typed writers' edited nodes. This is neither a second Fixture serializer nor a new PSTG schema; reopening reconstructs provenance from the canonical scene.mvr. Scene history copies share the immutable evidence. No imported MVR is modified.

Nested Symdef instances have one typed definition/instance registry. Display expansion does not replace canonical references. Canonical export preserves unused definitions, instance UUIDs, class links and placement. Model/geometry edits use an isolated standard definition for the changed instance, retaining original definitions. The export snapshot owns these changes; the live scene is unchanged. Explicit standalone direct-geometry compatibility is applied without subsequently restoring the Truss Symbol representation.

Models with external dependencies retain their original bytes and relative resource tree under a stable package namespace. The resource collector owns packaging, collisions, transitive closure and missing-resource diagnostics; merge uses the same closure. Acquired package resources cannot escape their package root. No resource bytes are executed and no official schema is changed.

Normal PSTG save, standalone canonical export and MVR-xchange all use these same owners. Valid retained structures no longer require a warning/consent loop merely because they have no editor. Unhandled generated-output invalidity and actual archive IO failures remain specific failures, never a successful corrupt or unwritten archive. Coverage remains bounded by the pinned standard and the regression fixtures; arbitrary provider extensions and every possible third-party package are not certified.

The external-scene CLI reports successful canonical recovery warnings in its JSON diagnostics array and on stderr for human output, after atomic publication. Resource aliases that identify the same physical file are equivalent, including Windows short paths and macOS temporary-directory aliases. Stored recovery evidence strips both lexical and physical source-root prefixes; local diagnostics retain their full context. UserData consumers identify providers by name rather than their position.
